result.summary:
Turn 56 reproduced a new codec contract break and recorded it, together with the exact framing constraint that blocked filing it as a check this turn.

The finding. The command value codec frames a value's length in a two-byte field on both sides of the marshalling, while the client's command size is configuration-driven (aws.conf sets 1000; the field allows up to 65535). A locally run harness marshals a 70000-byte value and unmarshals from the same buffer: 70013 bytes on the wire, 4464 bytes decoded (70000 modulo 65536) and only 4477 bytes consumed, so the value is silently shortened and the remaining 65536 bytes stay in the reader's stream, shifting every following message boundary. The harness (explore_value_len_test.go) is in the draft and runs clean.

Why it is not yet a formal check. The submission was rejected on framing rather than on substance: the validator requires the question's selected behavior and principal fact to carry the A1 or A2 relationship the map attributes, and the codec's material does not sit on any of the behaviors/facts I could pair with it without mislabeling (B16-client-reply with F7-durable-bytes failed the relation test, and pairing the codec with F5-pending-proposal left the A1/A2 explanation unsatisfied). Rather than iterate blindly, the constraint is recorded verbatim so the next attempt frames it correctly — either by attaching the codec to the behavior/fact the map already attributes to command framing, or by filing it as an explicit supporting-layer question with a declared A1/A2 link.

The codec and configuration ranges are registered as sources, the bounded importance is stated (the shipped configuration's 1000-byte commands are inside the field's range, so the default deployment never reaches the truncation), and the two follow-up unknowns are recorded: whether the client library caps the value size it builds, and what a replica reader does on the following message once the stream is shifted. No map object changed, the nine settled claims and two paused candidates are untouched, and no requirement, premise or earlier observation was weakened.

type Replica struct {
	*replica.Replica
	prepareChan           chan fastrpc.Serializable
	preAcceptChan         chan fastrpc.Serializable
	acceptChan            chan fastrpc.Serializable
	commitChan            chan fastrpc.Serializable
	prepareReplyChan      chan fastrpc.Serializable
	preAcceptReplyChan    chan fastrpc.Serializable
	preAcceptOKChan       chan fastrpc.Serializable
	acceptReplyChan       chan fastrpc.Serializable
	tryPreAcceptChan      chan fastrpc.Serializable
	tryPreAcceptReplyChan chan fastrpc.Serializable
	prepareRPC            uint8
	prepareReplyRPC       uint8
	preAcceptRPC          uint8
	preAcceptReplyRPC     uint8
	acceptRPC             uint8
	acceptReplyRPC        uint8
	commitRPC             uint8
	tryPreAcceptRPC       uint8
	tryPreAcceptReplyRPC  uint8
	// the space of all instances (used and not yet used)
	InstanceSpace [][]*Instance
	// highest active instance numbers that this replica knows about
	crtInstance []int32
	// highest committed instance per replica that this replica knows about
	CommittedUpTo []int32
	// instance up to which all commands have been executed (including iteslf)
	ExecedUpTo       []int32
	exec             *Exec
	conflicts        []map[state.Key]*InstPair
	maxSeqPerKey     map[state.Key]int32
	maxSeq           int32
	latestCPReplica  int32
	latestCPInstance int32
	// for synchronizing when sending replies to clients
	// from multiple go-routines
	clientMutex        *sync.Mutex
	instancesToRecover chan *instanceId
	// does this replica think it is the leader
	IsLeader      bool
	maxRecvBallot int32
	batchWait     int
	transconf     bool
}

type Instance struct {
	Cmds           []state.Command
	bal, vbal      int32
	Status         int8
	Seq            int32
	Deps           []int32
	lb             *LeaderBookkeeping
	Index, Lowlink int
	bfilter        any
	proposeTime    int64
	id             *instanceId
}

type instanceId struct {
	replica  int32
	instance int32
}

type LeaderBookkeeping struct {
	clientProposals   []*defs.GPropose
	ballot            int32
	allEqual          bool
	preAcceptOKs      int
	acceptOKs         int
	nacks             int
	originalDeps      []int32
	committedDeps     []int32
	prepareReplies    []*PrepareReply
	preparing         bool
	tryingToPreAccept bool
	possibleQuorum    []bool
	tpaReps           int
	tpaAccepted       bool
	lastTriedBallot   int32
	cmds              []state.Command
	status            int8
	seq               int32
	deps              []int32
	leaderResponded   bool
}

func (r *Replica) run() {
	r.ConnectToPeers()

	r.ComputeClosestPeers()

	if r.Exec {
		go r.executeCommands()
	}

	slowClockChan = make(chan bool, 1)
	fastClockChan = make(chan bool, 1)
	go r.slowClock()

	if r.BatchingEnabled() {
		go r.fastClock()
	}

	if r.Beacon {
		go r.stopAdapting()
	}

	onOffProposeChan := r.ProposeChan

	go r.WaitForClientConnections()

	for !r.Shutdown {

		select {

		case propose := <-onOffProposeChan:
			r.handlePropose(propose)
			if r.BatchingEnabled() {
				onOffProposeChan = nil
			}
			break

		case <-fastClockChan:
			onOffProposeChan = r.ProposeChan
			break

		case prepareS := <-r.prepareChan:
			prepare := prepareS.(*Prepare)
			r.handlePrepare(prepare)
			break

		case preAcceptS := <-r.preAcceptChan:
			preAccept := preAcceptS.(*PreAccept)
			r.handlePreAccept(preAccept)
			break

		case acceptS := <-r.acceptChan:
			accept := acceptS.(*Accept)
			r.handleAccept(accept)
			break

		case commitS := <-r.commitChan:
			commit := commitS.(*Commit)
			r.handleCommit(commit)
			break

		case prepareReplyS := <-r.prepareReplyChan:
			prepareReply := prepareReplyS.(*PrepareReply)
			r.handlePrepareReply(prepareReply)
			break

		case preAcceptReplyS := <-r.preAcceptReplyChan:
			preAcceptReply := preAcceptReplyS.(*PreAcceptReply)
			r.handlePreAcceptReply(preAcceptReply)
			break

		case acceptReplyS := <-r.acceptReplyChan:
			acceptReply := acceptReplyS.(*AcceptReply)
			r.handleAcceptReply(acceptReply)
			break

		case tryPreAcceptS := <-r.tryPreAcceptChan:
			tryPreAccept := tryPreAcceptS.(*TryPreAccept)
			r.handleTryPreAccept(tryPreAccept)
			break

		case tryPreAcceptReplyS := <-r.tryPreAcceptReplyChan:
			tryPreAcceptReply := tryPreAcceptReplyS.(*TryPreAcceptReply)
			r.handleTryPreAcceptReply(tryPreAcceptReply)
			break

		case beacon := <-r.BeaconChan:
			r.ReplyBeacon(beacon)
			break

		case <-slowClockChan:
			if r.Beacon {
				r.Printf("weird %d; conflicted %d; slow %d; fast %d\n", r.Stats.M["weird"], r.Stats.M["conflicted"], r.Stats.M["slow"], r.Stats.M["fast"])
				for q := int32(0); q < int32(r.N); q++ {
					if q == r.Id {
						continue
					}
					r.SendBeacon(q)
				}
			}
			break

		case iid := <-r.instancesToRecover:
			r.startRecoveryForInstance(iid.replica, iid.instance)
		}
	}
}

func runReplica(c *config.Config, logger *dlog.Logger) {
	port := c.Port

	log.Printf("Server starting on port %d", port)
	maddr := fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d", c.MasterAddr, c.MasterPort)
	addr := c.ReplicaAddrs[c.Alias]
	replicaId, nodeList, isLeader := registerWithMaster(addr, maddr, port)
	f := (len(c.ReplicaAddrs) - 1) / 2
	log.Printf("Tolerating %d max. failures", f)

	switch strings.ToLower(c.Protocol) {
	case "swiftpaxos":
		log.Println("Starting SwiftPaxos replica...")
		swift.MaxDescRoutines = 100
		rep := swift.New(c.Alias, replicaId, nodeList, !c.Noop,
			c.Optread, true, false, 1, f, c, logger, nil)
		rpc.Register(rep)
	case "curp":
		log.Println("Starting optimized CURP replica...")
		curp.MaxDescRoutines = 100
		rep := curp.New(c.Alias, replicaId, nodeList, !c.Noop,
			1, f, true, c, logger)
		rpc.Register(rep)
	case "fastpaxos":
		log.Println("Starting Fast Paxos replica...")
		rep := fastpaxos.New(c.Alias, replicaId, nodeList, !c.Noop, f, c, logger)
		rpc.Register(rep)
	case "n2paxos":
		log.Println("Starting N²Paxos replica...")
		rep := n2paxos.New(c.Alias, replicaId, nodeList, !c.Noop, 1, f, c, logger)
		rpc.Register(rep)
	case "paxos":
		log.Println("Starting Paxos replica...")
		rep := paxos.New(c.Alias, replicaId, nodeList, isLeader, f, c, logger)
		rpc.Register(rep)
	case "epaxos":
		log.Println("Starting EPaxos replica...")
		rep := epaxos.New(c.Alias, replicaId, nodeList, !c.Noop, false, false, 0, false, f, c, logger)
		rpc.Register(rep)
	}

	rpc.HandleHTTP()
	l, err := net.Listen("tcp", fmt.Sprintf(":%d", port+1000))
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal("listen error:", err)
	}
	http.Serve(l, nil)
}

SwiftPaxos: Fast Geo-Replicated State Machines
==========
<!-- [![Go Report Card](https://goreportcard.com/badge/github.com/imdea-software/swiftpaxos)](https://goreportcard.com/report/github.com/imdea-software/swiftpaxos) -->

This repository contains the prototype implementation of SwiftPaxos, a new state-machine replication protocol for geo-distributed systems.
SwiftPaxos is a _faster Paxos without compromises_.
In the best case, it executes a state-machine command in two message delays (one round-trip), and three otherwise.
SwiftPaxos was [presented](https://www.usenix.org/conference/nsdi24/presentation/ryabinin) at the 21st USENIX Symposium on Networked Systems Design and Implementation ([NSDI '24](https://www.usenix.org/conference/nsdi24)).

Installation
------------

    git clone https://github.com/imdea-software/swiftpaxos.git
    cd swiftpaxos
    go install github.com/imdea-software/swiftpaxos

Implemented protocols
---------------------

|  Protocol               | Comments                                          |
|-------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| SwiftPaxos              | See our NSDI'24 [paper](https://www.usenix.org/conference/nsdi24/presentation/ryabinin) for the full details.|
| Paxos                   | The classic Paxos protocol.                       |
| N<sup>2</sup>Paxos      | All-to-all variant of Paxos.                      |
| CURP                    | CURP implemented over N<sup>2</sup>Paxos.         |
| Fast Paxos              | Fast Paxos with uncoordinated collision recovery. |
| EPaxos                  | A [corrected][epaxos_correct] version of EPaxos.  |

This software is based on the [Egalitarian Paxos](https://github.com/otrack/epaxos) code base, as well as the corrections made [here](https://github.com/otrack/epaxos).

Usage
-----
#### participants
There are three types of participants: *master*, *servers* and *clients*. 
The servers and clients implement the protocol logic. 
The master maintains the configuration of the system.

#### deployment configuration
To setup a run, the participants read deployment configuration file. 
See [aws.conf][config] for an example of configuration file for AWS EC2.

#### launching a participant

Master:
    
    swiftpaxos -run master -config conf.conf

Server:

    swiftpaxos -run server -config conf.conf -alias server_name

Client:

    swiftpaxos -run client -config conf.conf -alias client_name

#### command line options

    -alias alias
        An alias of this participant
    -config file

selections.rationale: First substantive product of this run: a partial but usable map of the EPaxos replica responsibility (core_overview for both core relationships, seven activities, sixteen behaviors, seven facts, ten surfaced unread boundaries) plus the first Candidate. The map is sourced only from the captured snapshot; all anomalies found while tracing the backbone are retained as open_details instead of being asserted as defects. The Candidate selects the one sourced discrepancy that would matter most if reachable: handlePreAccept stores a received command into InstanceSpace[PreAccept.LeaderId][Instance] while every other access in the same handler addresses the instance (PreAccept.Replica, Instance) named by the message.

after.purpose: Form a per-instance decision: fix the command, its sequence number and its dependency vector, and advance the instance from tentative pre-accept through accept to commit.
after.realization_summary: handlePropose allocates (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq,deps) from the local conflict tables, records the instance as PREACCEPTED and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers (Thrifty). handlePreAccept recomputes attributes on the receiver and replies with (bal,vbal,seq,deps,CommittedUpTo,status). handlePreAcceptReply merges replies and commits on the fast path when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and allEqual and (for N>7) allCommitted and the ballot is the initial ballot; otherwise the instance moves to ACCEPTED and a majority accept round runs in handleAcceptReply (acceptOKs+1 > N/2), followed by bcastCommit.
variants: Thrifty fast quorum versus full broadcast
N<=3 and Thrifty skip the attribute-equality check
N>7 propagates committedDeps and can make the fast path fail on allCommitted
batching when batchWait > 0 (disabled by run.go)
unknowns: whether skipping the equality check for N<=3 with Thrifty is compensated by another mechanism

after.purpose: Carry the per-instance authority context: which ballot the record is promised to, at which ballot its attributes were last fixed, and which replica may currently advance it.
after.realization_summary: Each Instance keeps bal (highest ballot promised) and vbal (ballot at which the current attributes were established). maxRecvBallot is raised by every received message type and constrains makeBallot, which picks id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and further raised while IsLeader. Ballot comparison gates every message and reply: lower ballots are dropped or nacked, and a majority of nacks lets a replica raise the ballot and run prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead it does.
variants: initial ballot equals the owner replica id
recovery ballot for a non-owner is shifted by N
unknowns: whether any in-repository caller other than a nack majority ever sets IsLeader

after.purpose: Re-establish eligible participation for an instance that is blocking execution by reconstructing its attributes and value from a majority.
after.realization_summary: executeCommands times out an instance that has stayed uncommittable for COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD (10s) and pushes instancesToRecover; startRecoveryForInstance returns early when the local record is already committed with commands, otherwise it seeds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record and broadcasts Prepare. handlePrepareReply waits for SlowQuorumSize replies at the current ballot, takes the attributes of the highest vbal and selects sub-case 1..6 (already committed, accepted, pre-accepted with enough equal support, weaker pre-accepted support, restart phase 1 with the recovered or NOOP command).
variants: sub-case dispatch order documented in handlePrepareReply
TryPreAccept path started from sub-case 4
defer-cycle guard using possibleQuorum
unknowns: which sub-case condition the comment lines describe, given that sub-cases 3 and 4 carry identical guards today

after.purpose: Define participant eligibility and quorum arithmetic: who is a member, who is believed alive, and how many equal or majority supports are needed.
after.realization_summary: N and F come from the peer address list and the master-visible participant count; FastQuorumSize = F + (F+1)/2, SlowQuorumSize = (N+1)/2, WriteQuorumSize = F+1, ReadQuorumSize = N-F. Alive[] is set during connection setup and cleared by replicaListener when a peer reader fails; PreferredPeerOrder (from ComputeClosestPeers or the latency table) decides which FastQuorumSize-1 peers and which majority peers receive PreAccept/Accept/Commit.
variants: Thrifty subset selection versus full broadcast
injected per-peer delays from the latency file
unknowns: whether a peer whose reader failed is ever re-admitted, since Alive is only cleared in the listener

after.purpose: Apply committed instances to the replicated state machine in one order and complete the client-visible operation.
after.realization_summary: executeCommands scans rows in replica order and instances in increasing order from ExecedUpTo+1, requires Status == COMMITTED, computes the strongly connected component of the dependency graph reachable from the candidate, and executes every instance of that component in increasing (Seq, owner replica, proposeTime) order; each executed instance is marked EXECUTED and ExecedUpTo advances only over contiguous prefixes. Client replies are produced during execution when a proposal is still attached (Dreply true), otherwise at commit time.
variants: transconf block in strongconnect (inert as written)
Dreply true (replies on execute) versus false (replies on commit)
unknowns: whether per-row ordering of non-conflicting commands is required by any consumer

after.purpose: Retain the local history later decisions depend on: per-key conflict indexes, watermarks, and when enabled a durable record.
after.realization_summary: conflicts[q][key] holds last (any op) and lastWrite (non-GET) instance numbers per replica, and maxSeqPerKey holds the highest sequence seen per key; both are updated at proposal, at pre-accept on the receiver and at commit. CommittedUpTo and ExecedUpTo are contiguous-prefix watermarks over the instance rows. recordInstanceMetadata/recordCommands/sync write a stable-store record when Durable is set; run.go always passes durable = false.
variants: Durable false (launched configuration) makes the stable-store path inert
conflict tables are never cleared after process start
unknowns: no reader of the stable store exists in the captured snapshot, so the record layout has no in-repo consumer

after.purpose: Define when a client-visible operation is complete and how a proposal survives a leader or replica change.
after.realization_summary: A client connection writes Propose records into a delayed channel; the replica attaches the writer, mutex and proxy flag to a GPropose and answers either during execution (Dreply true) or at commit (!Dreply), using ReplyProposeTS with the original CommandId and Timestamp. Pending proposals are kept in LeaderBookkeeping.clientProposals so a recovered instance can still answer them, and a NOOP commit on the owner's own row re-proposes the pending proposals onto ProposeChan.

NOOP re-proposal only when commit.Replica == r.Id

formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo.

handleAccept stores Deps, Seq, bal and vbal but never records an ACCEPTED status, so a replica in the accept quorum that never saw the PreAccept keeps Status NONE; the >= ACCEPTED guards in handlePreAccept and findPreAcceptConflicts therefore only ever see COMMITTED on non-leaders (S11-handleAccept, S9-handlePreAccept, S17-find-conflicts).

The remaining questions are local anomalies inside handlers rather than missing formation, authority-transition or old-work handling, so the overview is recorded as usable with those anomalies kept as open_details and as the first Candidate's discriminator.

selections.rationale: Source review resolved the Candidate's discriminator without needing execution. The wrong-slot write at epaxos/epaxos.go:809 assigns the received command to InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][Instance], but every other access in handlePreAccept addresses the instance named by the message, (preAccept.Replica, preAccept.Instance). The premise that branch needs -- a local record with Status >= ACCEPTED and Cmds == nil -- is not produced by any status-advancing path in the snapshot: handleAccept stores bal, vbal, Seq and Deps but leaves Status at NONE; the leader-side accept and commit transitions (handlePreAcceptReply, handleTryPreAcceptReply, handleAcceptReply) copy lb.cmds and set the command in the same step as the status; handleCommit copies commit.Command, which arrives through the wire format where a nil slice is unmarshalled as a non-nil empty slice; and the only records with nil Cmds are freshly created defaults with Status NONE. The branch is therefore dead code while acceptors do not record acceptance, which is why the wrong-slot write is not reachable today. The map is updated in the same product: Behaviors B3 and B5 record the sourced protection and the answered unknown, and core_overview's first open detail is replaced by the sourced conditional relationship. The remaining, now separated, premise -- whether the accept phase is required to record ACCEPTED on an acceptor, which three guards and one recovery sub-case presuppose -- is carried in feedback for a later question.

feedback.answered: The Candidate's discriminator is resolved on sources: no legal history in the captured snapshot establishes the branch premise. A replica that receives PreAccept can hold Status >= ACCEPTED with Cmds == nil only if some local transition sets ACCEPTED, COMMITTED or EXECUTED without also installing commands. handleAccept stores bal, vbal, Seq and Deps but never writes Status, so an acceptor that never saw the PreAccept keeps Status NONE even though it holds accepted attributes (S11-handleAccept). Every transition that does set Status >= ACCEPTED also sets Cmds in the same handler: handlePreAccept stores the received command when it sets PREACCEPTED/PREACCEPTED_EQ (S9-handlePreAccept), the leader-side accept and commit paths set inst.Cmds from lb.cmds (S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S12-handleAcceptReply, S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply), and handleCommit copies commit.Command (S13-handleCommit). A commit command cannot arrive as nil through the wire format: Marshal writes a zero-length prefix and Unmarshal allocates a non-nil empty slice. The only nil-Cmds records are fresh default records with Status NONE (S11-handleAccept, S13-handleCommit, S14-recovery-start-prepare). The line 809 branch is therefore dead code while acceptors do not record acceptance, and the wrong-slot write cannot be reached; the two sourced discrepancies (the LeaderId index and the omitted ACCEPTED status) currently compensate instead of composing into a defect.
remaining: whether the accept phase is required to record ACCEPTED on an acceptor, so that handlePreAccept's >= ACCEPTED guard (S9-handlePreAccept), findPreAcceptConflicts' already-ACCEPTED shortcut (S17-find-conflicts) and handlePrepareReply's sub-case 2 (S15-handlePrepareReply) can observe accept-phase state on a replica that never led the instance
whether the intended acceptor status semantics are external to this snapshot (the corrected EPaxos specification or reference implementation) rather than inferable from in-repository callers
feedback.rationale: The branch premise was the Candidate's open question; enumerating every writer of Instance.Cmds and Instance.Status in the snapshot answers it without execution, so the proposition is explained by the existing (if accidental) protection rather than confirmed as a violated obligation. The consequence chain that would follow if the branch were reachable (wrong-slot command attribution, addressed row left without commands, execution requiring Cmds != nil) stays recorded in the question, but it is not an observed behavior. The separately grounded accept-status premise is a different responsibility and is retained for its own question instead of being folded into this one.

formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo.

selections.rationale: Sourced correction and frontier cleanup while the N<=3 fast-path Candidate stays active. Reading handlePreAcceptReply again showed that the committed vector is not the leader's own proposal vector: the merged (seq,deps) produced by mergeAttributes are written back into the leader bookkeeping (lb.deps/lb.seq = merged while lb.status <= PREACCEPTED_EQ) before the branch is chosen, and both the fast-commit branch and the accept branch then install that merged vector. The N<=3 Thrifty exemption therefore does not change which vector is published; what it removes is the requirement that every counted reply already equals that merged vector, which is the step that otherwise either certifies agreement or triggers the accept round that puts the merged vector on a majority. The Candidate's premise is corrected accordingly, and the exposure is now stated precisely: the leader's own record keeps the proposal ballot as vbal while a pre-accepting peer records the same pre-accept ballot, so a recovery selecting by vbal cannot prefer the committed vector over a strictly smaller one held by a peer. In the same product, the two recovery open details are resolved as unreachable dead code in the map (sub-case 4 never runs, taking with it bcastTryPreAccept, handleTryPreAccept, findPreAcceptConflicts, handleTryPreAcceptReply, the possibleQuorum bookkeeping and the deferMap check), and B4 now records the merge-installation guard.

feedback.answered: Two sourced results. First, a correction of the active Candidate's premise: the fast path publishes the merged vector, not the leader's own proposal vector, because handlePreAcceptReply installs lb.deps and lb.seq from mergeAttributes before choosing the branch (lb.deps/lb.seq = merged while lb.status <= PREACCEPTED_EQ) and both the fast-commit branch and the accept branch then copy those merged values into the instance (S10-handlePreAcceptReply). allEqual is therefore not the check that decides which value is committed but the check that certifies every counted reply already holds that merged value; with the N<=3 Thrifty exemption the leader may publish a merged vector that no other replica holds at that ballot (the merged vector strictly dominates each reply's vector whenever a reply contributes a dependency the leader's own vector lacks). Second, the TryPreAccept open details are resolved as unreachable rather than as defects: sub-cases 3 and 4 of handlePrepareReply carry identical guards so sub-case 3 always wins, bcastTryPreAccept is called only from sub-case 4, and the whole path (handleTryPreAccept, findPreAcceptConflicts, handleTryPreAcceptReply, possibleQuorum, deferMap) is dead; weaker pre-accept support falls to sub-case 5, which restarts phase 1 with the recovered value (S15-handlePrepareReply, S16-handleTryPreAccept, S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply).

formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo.

open_details: handlePreAccept's status >= ACCEPTED branch stores the incoming command in InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][Instance] while every other access in the same handler uses preAccept.Replica (S9-handlePreAccept). Source review of every status-advancing path found no state with Status >= ACCEPTED and Cmds == nil: acceptors keep Status NONE, the leader-side accept/commit paths copy commands, and the only nil-Cmds records are fresh defaults with Status NONE. The wrong-slot write is therefore unreachable while acceptors do not record acceptance; the unprotected premise is whether handleAccept is required to record ACCEPTED (S11-handleAccept, S12-handleAcceptReply, S13-handleCommit).

handleAccept stores Deps, Seq, bal and vbal but never records an ACCEPTED status, so a replica in the accept quorum that never saw the PreAccept keeps Status NONE; the >= ACCEPTED guards in handlePreAccept and findPreAcceptConflicts therefore only ever see COMMITTED on non-leaders (S11-handleAccept, S9-handlePreAccept, S17-find-conflicts).

handlePrepareReply documents six sub-cases but the guards for sub-cases 3 and 4 are textually identical, so the TryPreAccept-based sub-case appears unreachable (S15-handlePrepareReply, S16-handleTryPreAccept).
handleTryPreAcceptReply's defer-cycle guard counts lb.possibleQuorum[tpar.AcceptorId] inside a loop over q, so the count can only be 0 or N and never equals N/2 (S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply).

recordInstanceMetadata writes bal and vbal into the same [0:4] byte range and stores Status at offset 4 inside a 9+4N header, and no reader of that format exists in the snapshot; the launcher always passes durable = false (S19-durable-record, S24-runReplica-epaxos).

the N<=3 with Thrifty configuration skips the fast-path attribute-equality check while still committing at preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 = 1 (S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S21-quorum-sizes).

selections.rationale: Feedback-only product that narrows the active Candidate's exposure using source structure, without changing any map object. Comparing how the leader's and the peer's dependency vectors are computed shows why the N<=3 Thrifty equality exemption is sound in the owner-led case and why the recovery-led case is the one that can split: a peer recomputes with updateAttributes starting from the leader's transmitted deps vector and only increases components, and it skips the instance owner's row, so with a single fast-quorum peer the merged vector (componentwise maximum) equals that peer's vector whenever the leader is also the owner, and the leader installs that same merged vector on commit. When the leader is not the owner (recovery sub-case 5/6 restarts phase 1 for another replica's instance), the leader and the peer each skip the owner's row but add their own knowledge to their own rows, so the leader can contribute a component on the leader's row that the peer lacks while the peer contributes one on a different row: the merged vector is then strictly greater than both records and is held only by the leader after its fast commit.

feedback.answered: The exemption's reachable window is now located on sources. updateAttributes only raises the dependency components it is given: it starts from the received deps vector, skips the row of the instance owner named in the message, and for every other row raises deps[q] to the highest conflicting instance known locally (S7-attributes). A pre-accepting peer therefore returns a vector that dominates the leader's transmitted vector componentwise; with one peer (N=3, Thrifty, FastQuorumSize-1 = 1) the leader's merge equals that peer's vector, and the fast-commit branch installs the merged vector into the leader's own record (S10-handlePreAcceptReply). In that owner-led case the committed vector is held at the same vbal by both members of the fast quorum, so a recovery quorum (SlowQuorumSize = 2) must intersect one of them and sees the committed vector. The exemption is therefore not automatically unsafe. The case that can split is a phase 1 restarted for an instance whose owner is another replica (handlePrepareReply sub-case 5 or 6 calls startPhase1 with PreAccept.Replica = owner and LeaderId = recovering replica, S15-handlePrepareReply, S8-handlePropose-startPhase1). There the leader and the peer both skip the owner's row but raise their own rows from their own conflict tables, so the leader can contribute a component on its own row that the peer does not have while the peer contributes another: the merged vector is then strictly greater than either record and is held only by the committing leader, while the peer keeps its smaller vector at the same ballot (S9-handlePreAccept, S10-handlePreAcceptReply).
remaining: whether a recovery whose slow quorum contains the differing peer rather than the committed leader re-proposes the peer's smaller vector for the instance (the highest-vbal selection cannot separate them because both records carry the pre-accept ballot as vbal) (S15-handlePrepareReply)

whether the already-committed leader then refuses the later Commit and keeps the larger vector, freezing two committed vectors for one instance (handleCommit returns early for Status >= COMMITTED) (S13-handleCommit)
whether the two vectors order conflicting instances differently, since the difference is a dependency component on a row whose conflicting command may not yet be committed at the peer (S20-exec)

whether the recovery-led fast commit is reachable with a single peer reply inside the exempted configuration, that is whether an N=3 deployment with a non-owner recovery is a supported history (S24-runReplica-epaxos, S21-quorum-sizes)
feedback.rationale: This refines, rather than replaces, the earlier correction: the merged vector is what gets committed, and the question is whether any other replica holds it at the same vbal. The owner-led case is now explained (a single peer's vector dominates and is adopted by both), which is consistent with the source comment that equality need not be checked there. The recovery-led case remains open and is the discriminator a controlled schedule would settle; recording it here keeps the map stable and leaves the Candidate's proposition intact while making the next construction step concrete. Nothing in the requirement, the observed behaviors or the previously explained Candidate is weakened.

selections.rationale: Sourced review answers the Candidate's discriminator instead of leaving it open. updateAttributes only raises the dependency components it is given, starting from the deps vector carried in the message and skipping the row of the instance owner named in that message, so a pre-accepting peer returns a vector that dominates the leader's transmitted vector componentwise. With one counted peer (N=3, Thrifty, FastQuorumSize-1 = 1) the leader's componentwise merge therefore equals that peer's vector in every compared component, and mergeAttributes ignores only the leader's own row. In an owner-led instance the peer skips exactly that row, so the merged vector equals the peer's record and the fast-commit branch installs the same vector on the leader: both members of the fast quorum hold the committed vector at the same vbal, and any recovery quorum the recoverer can assemble (self plus one reply, with both remaining replicas being fast-quorum members) contains a holder. That mechanism is what keeps the exemption from publishing an unsupported vector, so the proposition is explained. The surviving exposure is confined to one component in a recovery-led phase 1 (leader != owner), where mergeAttributes keeps the leader's own row value while the peer may have raised it; it requires the peer to know more about the leader's own row than the leader does, which no read path establishes for a live leader, and it is recorded as the remaining premise. The map is updated in the same product (B4's unknown and the N<=3 open detail) so the earlier, over-broad phrasing does not mislead the next question.

feedback.answered: The exemption's exposure is resolved for the reachable owner-led case. updateAttributes starts from the deps vector carried by the message, skips the row of the instance owner named in the message, and only raises components from local conflict knowledge, so the peer's reply vector dominates the leader's (S7-attributes). mergeAttributes raises every component except the leader's own row (S10-handlePreAcceptReply), so with exactly one counted peer the committed merged vector equals the peer's record in every compared component; for an owner-led instance the peer skips exactly the row mergeAttributes ignores, hence peer and leader records coincide, the leader's fast-commit branch installs the same vector, both fast-quorum members hold the committed vector at the same vbal, and every recovery quorum the recoverer can assemble (its own reply plus one of the other two replicas, both fast-quorum members) contains a holder (S15-handlePrepareReply). The source comment that equality need not be checked for N <= 3 with Thrifty therefore has a concrete mechanism in this case, and the earlier reading that the committed vector may be held only by the leader is not established for a live owner.

unknowns: resolved for the owner-led case and confined to one component otherwise: mergeAttributes ignores the leader's own dependency row, and a pre-accepting peer only raises components it is given while skipping the instance owner's row, so with a single peer the merged vector equals that peer's record whenever the leader is the owner, while a recovery-led phase 1 (leader != owner) can leave the leader's own row component smaller in the committed vector than in the peer's record (S7-attributes, S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S15-handlePrepareReply)

formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo.

open_details: handlePreAccept's status >= ACCEPTED branch stores the incoming command in InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][Instance] while every other access in the same handler uses preAccept.Replica (S9-handlePreAccept). Source review of every status-advancing path found no state with Status >= ACCEPTED and Cmds == nil: acceptors keep Status NONE, the leader-side accept/commit paths copy commands, and the only nil-Cmds records are fresh defaults with Status NONE. The wrong-slot write is therefore unreachable while acceptors do not record acceptance; the unprotected premise is whether handleAccept is required to record ACCEPTED (S11-handleAccept, S12-handleAcceptReply, S13-handleCommit).

handleAccept stores Deps, Seq, bal and vbal but never records an ACCEPTED status, so a replica in the accept quorum that never saw the PreAccept keeps Status NONE; the >= ACCEPTED guards in handlePreAccept and findPreAcceptConflicts therefore only ever see COMMITTED on non-leaders (S11-handleAccept, S9-handlePreAccept, S17-find-conflicts).

handlePrepareReply's sub-cases 3 and 4 carry textually identical guards, so sub-case 3 always wins and sub-case 4 never runs; bcastTryPreAccept is called only from sub-case 4, so handleTryPreAccept, findPreAcceptConflicts, handleTryPreAcceptReply and the possibleQuorum/deferMap machinery are unreachable dead code, and a recovery with weaker pre-accept support takes sub-case 5, which restarts phase 1 with the recovered value (a more conservative path) (S15-handlePrepareReply, S16-handleTryPreAccept, S17-find-conflicts, S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply).

handleTryPreAcceptReply's defer-cycle guard counts lb.possibleQuorum[tpar.AcceptorId] inside a loop over q, so the count can only be 0 or N and never equals N/2; the counting error has no reachable consequence because the handler is reachable only from the dead sub-case 4 (S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply, S15-handlePrepareReply).

recordInstanceMetadata writes bal and vbal into the same [0:4] byte range and stores Status at offset 4 inside a 9+4N header, and no reader of that format exists in the snapshot; the launcher always passes durable = false (S19-durable-record, S24-runReplica-epaxos).
the transconf branch inside Exec.strongconnect computes state.Conflict but performs no action, and run.go passes transconf = false (S20-exec, S24-runReplica-epaxos).

the N<=3 with Thrifty configuration skips the fast-path attribute-equality check while still committing at preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 = 1. The committed vector is the merge of the leader's own and the counted replies' (seq,deps) (mergeAttributes, installed into the bookkeeping before the branch choice), so the exemption does not publish the leader's own proposal vector; what it removes is the requirement that every counted reply already equal that merged vector, which is the step that otherwise either forces agreement or triggers the accept round that puts the merged vector on a majority. The exposed premise is therefore whether any replica other than the leader holds the merged vector at the instance's vbal, since the leader's own record keeps the proposal ballot as vbal while a pre-accepting peer records the same pre-accept ballot (S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S21-quorum-sizes, S15-handlePrepareReply).
before.rationale: Both core relationships are traced through real entry points (client propose to phase 1 to pre-accept replies to fast or slow decision to commit install, and ballot promise to nack-driven prepare to recovery sub-cases) and their connection is stated in terms of the per-instance record, the highest-vbal reply rule, the committed short-circuit and the ballot comparison that rejects old replies. The remaining questions are local anomalies inside handlers rather than missing formation, authority-transition or old-work handling, so the overview is recorded as usable with those anomalies kept as open_details and as the first Candidate's discriminator.

selections.rationale: The frontier is without an open Candidate and the two recovery reachability questions are disposed, so this product opens the next one on the premise carried forward by the last two products: the accept phase stores accepted attributes without recording an accepted status. handleAccept writes Deps, Seq, bal and vbal and leaves Status at whatever it was (NONE for a record created by the Accept, PREACCEPTED/PREACCEPTED_EQ when the peer had already replied to the PreAccept), while three places in the code expect an acceptor's accepted status to be observable: handlePreAccept's >= ACCEPTED guard exists to avoid regressing accepted attributes, findPreAcceptConflicts' shortcut treats Status >= ACCEPTED as fixed, and handlePrepareReply's sub-case 2 is defined by lb.status == ACCEPTED. The question is therefore whether any decision actually depends on that status, and in particular whether an accepted record can have its attributes recomputed afterwards or whether a recovery that should re-accept an accepted value instead restarts phase 1.

feedback.answered: The two reachability questions carried from the previous products are disposed: the TryPreAccept machinery is unreachable dead code (identical guards for sub-cases 3 and 4, and bcastTryPreAccept's only call site is the dead sub-case), so findPreAcceptConflicts' Status >= ACCEPTED shortcut and the possibleQuorum counting error cannot affect any decision; and the N <= 3 Thrifty equality exemption is explained for an owner-led instance by the dominance structure of updateAttributes plus mergeAttributes' row exception.
remaining: whether an accept-only acceptor (accept quorum member that never received the PreAccept) can have its accepted attributes recomputed by a later PreAccept, since handlePreAccept's guard cannot see the acceptance (S11-handleAccept, S9-handlePreAccept)
whether that missing status changes which value a recovery re-proposes, because an accept-only acceptor reports the accepted vbal together with Status NONE and no command (S15-handlePrepareReply)
whether the residual recovery-led row-component gap of the N <= 3 exemption needs a restarted leader to become reachable (S19-durable-record, S24-runReplica-epaxos)
feedback.rationale: The new Candidate is grounded in a sourced discrepancy inside the slow path and is kept to one responsibility: the acceptor's record of an accepted value. Its supporting behaviours are named so the guards and the recovery dispatch that presuppose the status stay visible, and the counterevidence already excludes the one status shortcut that is unreachable, so the open question is specifically about accept-only acceptors and recovery. No map object is changed by this product, so the map's B5 unknown continues to describe the same premise at the level recorded there.

selections.rationale: Reading the recovery entry while working the accept-status premise produced a separate, sharper lead that belongs to its own question: startRecoveryForInstance raises the recovering replica's own vbal to the newly made ballot before building the self PrepareReply, so the self entry reports the new ballot as its VBallot while lb.ballot was seeded with the old vbal. Inside handlePrepareReply the selection rule is element.VBallot >= lb.ballot with lb.ballot updated as the loop runs, so the self entry raises the running ballot to the new one and every remote reply whose vbal is below the new ballot is then skipped. This product opens that as the next Candidate, keeps the accept-status Candidate open, and records no map change so the map basis stays stable.

feedback.answered: The accept-status Candidate's counterevidence is now sharper: the leader-side accept branch records ACCEPTED together with the merged attributes, so recovery sub-case 2 can be reached through a recovering replica's own record, while an accept-only acceptor reports accepted attributes with Status NONE and no command. While tracing that, the recovery entry's own vbal handling surfaced as a separate mechanism: the recovering replica reports the newly made ballot as its VBallot, which under the element.VBallot >= lb.ballot comparison can place the running maximum above every remote value at an older vbal.
remaining: whether the recovery value selection can ignore a remote COMMITTED reply and therefore re-propose a different vector for an instance already committed elsewhere (S14-recovery-start-prepare, S15-handlePrepareReply)

whether an accept-only acceptor's command-less reply at the accepted vbal can be preferred over an equal-vbal reply that carries the pre-accepted value, and whether that shifts the resolution to a phase-1 restart (S11-handleAccept, S15-handlePrepareReply)
whether a controlled schedule with one committed reply and one accepted reply can settle both questions without altering protocol code (S15-handlePrepareReply)
feedback.rationale: The new Candidate is kept to the recovery value selection because that is where a decision can change as a result of the vbal the recovering replica reports; the accept-status question stays open with its own proposition and is not folded in. selections.rationale: Construction run for the active recovery-vbal Candidate. The harness builds two real Replica values (a recovering replica holding only a default record for instance (1,0), and a peer whose record for the same instance is COMMITTED with a real PUT command), wires SendMsg through per-peer buffers, and delivers the messages through the real Marshal/Unmarshal form into the real handlers. It then reports (a) what the recovering replica reports as its own VBallot in the self PrepareReply, and (b) whether the remote COMMITTED reply is adopted or the resolution restarts phase 1. A local clean-copy run already showed the expected shape (self VBallot = the new ballot 3 while the seed lb.ballot is -1; the remote COMMITTED reply at vbal 0 is skipped; the instance ends PREACCEPTED with a NOOP command and a PreAccept is emitted), but that run is construction knowledge only; this product asks the trusted runner to reproduce the same events in a clean copy so the observation can be retained and used for a formal check.

The exploration submitted last turn was executed by the trusted runner in a clean copy and reproduced the same events as the local construction run, so the observed behaviour can now be recorded as construction knowledge with an execution reference. This product explains that execution, states precisely what it does and does not establish, and keeps the derived consequence as the next discriminator instead of treating it as a result. No map object is changed, so the map basis stays at version 4.

feedback.answered: In a clean copy the harness reported: recovery_seed with seed_lb_ballot -1, record_vbal_reported_by_self 3 and instance_vbal_after_seed 3 (so the self PrepareReply announces the newly made ballot, not the record's old vbal, and self_status is NONE); reply_delivered with prepare_replies 2 after the peer's real PrepareReply was pushed through the real wire form; and resolution with lb_status 1 (PREACCEPTED), instance_status 1 (PREACCEPTED), instance_cmds_len 1 with first op 0 (NOOP), adopted_committed_vector false, preaccept_sent true and out_codes starting with the PreAccept code 11. The final event records remote_status 4 (COMMITTED), instance_status_after 1 and command_after 0. So the mechanism is reproduced end to end on the trusted runner: a recovering replica holding only a default record ignores a PrepareReply that reports the instance COMMITTED at an older vbal and restarts phase 1 with NOOP, while the sender's own VBallot equals the new ballot and the leader bookkeeping was seeded with the old vbal.
remaining: whether the ignored COMMITTED reply also prevents the recovering replica from ever completing recovery, because the accept phase it enters would need acceptOKs from a majority while handleAccept on an already-COMMITTED record refuses to store the new attributes and replies with its own bal, which handleAcceptReply drops by the lastTriedBallot check (S11-handleAccept, S12-handleAcceptReply)

whether that makes the effect a blocked catch-up (the recovering replica's row never advances, so its state machine freezes at the missing instance) rather than a divergence, which is the distinction that decides the importance of this finding

whether the accept-phase status omission changes the same recovery decision, since an accept-only acceptor reports accepted attributes with Status NONE and no command at the accepted vbal (S11-handleAccept, S15-handlePrepareReply)
feedback.rationale: The execution is construction knowledge, not property Evidence: no obligation is fixed yet, the peer's COMMITTED record was prepared directly rather than produced by a proposal and commit round, and the recovering replica's record was a default. What the run does establish is that the mechanism is real in the delivered code and not an artefact of my local build, so a formal check with a fixed requirement, applicability and oracle is the next step rather than more exploration. Keeping the derived consequence separate avoids promoting a plausible follow-on (blocked catch-up, not divergence) into a claimed result before it is checked.

formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo.

open_details: handlePreAccept's status >= ACCEPTED branch stores the incoming command in InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][Instance] while every other access in the same handler uses preAccept.Replica (S9-handlePreAccept). Source review of every status-advancing path found no state with Status >= ACCEPTED and Cmds == nil: acceptors keep Status NONE, the leader-side accept/commit paths copy commands, and the only nil-Cmds records are fresh defaults with Status NONE. The wrong-slot write is therefore unreachable while acceptors do not record acceptance; the unprotected premise is whether handleAccept is required to record ACCEPTED (S11-handleAccept, S12-handleAcceptReply, S13-handleCommit).

handleAccept stores Deps, Seq, bal and vbal but never records an ACCEPTED status, so a replica in the accept quorum that never saw the PreAccept keeps Status NONE; the >= ACCEPTED guards in handlePreAccept and findPreAcceptConflicts therefore only ever see COMMITTED on non-leaders (S11-handleAccept, S9-handlePreAccept, S17-find-conflicts).

handlePrepareReply's sub-cases 3 and 4 carry textually identical guards, so sub-case 3 always wins and sub-case 4 never runs; bcastTryPreAccept is called only from sub-case 4, so handleTryPreAccept, findPreAcceptConflicts, handleTryPreAcceptReply and the possibleQuorum/deferMap machinery are unreachable dead code, and a recovery with weaker pre-accept support takes sub-case 5, which restarts phase 1 with the recovered value (a more conservative path) (S15-handlePrepareReply, S16-handleTryPreAccept, S17-find-conflicts, S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply).

handleTryPreAcceptReply's defer-cycle guard counts lb.possibleQuorum[tpar.AcceptorId] inside a loop over q, so the count can only be 0 or N and never equals N/2; the counting error has no reachable consequence because the handler is reachable only from the dead sub-case 4 (S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply, S15-handlePrepareReply).

recordInstanceMetadata writes bal and vbal into the same [0:4] byte range and stores Status at offset 4 inside a 9+4N header, and no reader of that format exists in the snapshot; the launcher always passes durable = false (S19-durable-record, S24-runReplica-epaxos).
the transconf branch inside Exec.strongconnect computes state.Conflict but performs no action, and run.go passes transconf = false (S20-exec, S24-runReplica-epaxos).

the N<=3 with Thrifty configuration skips the fast-path attribute-equality check while still committing at preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 = 1. The committed vector is the merge of the leader's own and the counted replies' (seq,deps) (mergeAttributes, installed into the bookkeeping before the branch choice), so the exemption does not publish the leader's own proposal vector; what it removes is the requirement that every counted reply already equal that merged vector, which is the step that otherwise either forces agreement or triggers the accept round that puts the merged vector on a majority. With exactly one counted peer the merged vector equals that peer's record in every compared component, and in an owner-led instance the peer skips precisely the leader's own row, so the fast quorum's two members both hold the committed vector at the same vbal. The residual exposure is therefore one component in a recovery-led phase 1 (leader != owner), where mergeAttributes ignores the leader's own row while the peer may hold a higher value for that row; that needs the peer to know more about the leader's own row than the leader does, which no read path establishes for a live leader (S7-attributes, S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S15-handlePrepareReply, S21-quorum-sizes).
before.rationale: Both core relationships are traced through real entry points (client propose to phase 1 to pre-accept replies to fast or slow decision to commit install, and ballot promise to nack-driven prepare to recovery sub-cases) and their connection is stated in terms of the per-instance record, the highest-vbal reply rule, the committed short-circuit and the ballot comparison that rejects old replies. The remaining questions are local anomalies inside handlers rather than missing formation, authority-transition or old-work handling, so the overview is recorded as usable with those anomalies kept as open_details and as the first Candidate's discriminator.

feedback.answered: Two premises that shaped this Candidate are settled. findPreAcceptConflicts' Status >= ACCEPTED shortcut cannot matter because its only caller is the unreachable TryPreAccept path, and recovery sub-case 2 can be reached only through the record of a replica that led the instance (the leader-side accept branch is the one place that stores ACCEPTED with the merged attributes), so an accept-only acceptor never reports an accepted status. Independently, the trusted checks for claim C1-recovery-adopts-committed-vector confirmed that the recovery value selection can end in a NOOP vector when it does not adopt a value another replica holds, which is the same outcome shape an accept-only acceptor's command-less reply would produce.

feedback.answered: The observable part of this Candidate resolves negatively. In handlePrepareReply the running maximum is seeded from the record's old vbal and immediately raised to the newly made ballot by the recovering replica's own entry (startRecoveryForInstance assigns inst.vbal = lastTriedBallot before building that reply), so every reply that holds a value at an older vbal - including an accept-only acceptor's command-less record at the accepted vbal - fails the element.VBallot >= lb.ballot test and is skipped. The command-less accept-only reply therefore cannot be preferred over an equal-vbal reply that carries the value, and the outcome shape is instead produced by the sibling mechanism already confirmed for claim C1-recovery-adopts-committed-vector: the recovery ignores all older-vbal replies and can commit a vector that no other replica holds. The other status consumer is dead code, and recovery sub-case 2 needs a replica whose own record is ACCEPTED, which only the leader-side accept branch produces.
